cards.title: Loss of human connection is the biggest threat to kids, not AI
cards.body: A pediatrician argues that screens aren't destroying human connection—the real solution is spending more time talking openly with children. Amid tech worries, direct conversation remains the most powerful tool for child development.

cards.title: Why is a child saying 'Na-na, na-na-na!' so annoying?
cards.body: Readers explore the universal frustration behind this classic juvenile taunt. The question examines why this simple phrase triggers such strong reactions in parents.

cards.title: Halloween: ditching cynicism for pumpkins and family magic
cards.body: A parent reflects on embracing Halloween traditions like Day of the Dead and Samhain to create moments of connection with their kids. Celebrating autumn becomes an opportunity for family togetherness rather than commercialism.

cards.title: After my wife died, a football club showed extraordinary kindness
cards.body: A father recounts how his son's youth football club sent a care package years after he'd stopped playing, finding them at their new address. The gesture demonstrated the profound impact community can have on grieving families.

cards.title: A yearly tradition brings families together through homemade jam
cards.body: After her daughter moved out, a parent maintains connection through an annual ritual of harvesting fruit and making her mother's jam recipe. Simple traditions become anchors for family relationships across distances.

cards.title: Whose dream is it? Why we pursue music lessons
cards.body: Behind children's music lessons lies a complex web of parental regret, social admiration, and idealized self-images. Understanding these motivations helps parents make authentic choices for their kids.

cards.title: Why feeling like we belong matters so much
cards.body: Family science research shows that belonging isn't about location but the people, experiences, and traditions that create connection. Children thrive when they feel secure within their family and community.

cards.title: ADHD has three clashing definitions—all matter
cards.body: ADHD can be understood through clinical, biological, and social lenses, each offering different insights into the condition. Parents benefit from understanding these perspectives to support their children effectively.
